Subject: Segmentation scope checklist — Dedicated vs Private VPC follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Wanted to capture the key takeaways and next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive. High-level notes: 

- Primary requirement: Clearline will process PHI for a subset of workflows (patient intake parsing). You indicated those flows must not transit shared tenant networks and need customer-controlled key management.
- Two deployment options under consideration: Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed reserved GPUs with tenant isolation) vs Private VPC (customer VPC / private control plane).

Open questions we promised to clarify:
1) For Dedicated capacity, what data residency guarantees exist (logs, backups, diagnostics)?
2) For Private VPC, what parts of the control plane run in Clearline's VPC vs Redwood control plane?
3) Timeline and effort: estimated lead time for Private VPC onboarding and network runbook.

Attachments I’m including: vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (your legal asked for a completed questionnaire), SOC2-Summary.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 excerpt). I’ll also share a short privacy matrix and architecture diagram ahead of the tech call.

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus Lin (solutions engineer) to run a 45-min technical session Wed 6/17 or Thu 6/18 — please confirm preferred slot.
- Clara (legal) — if you can send any minimum contractual clauses (KMS, retention, audit) you need to see, we’ll bring pricing/contracting expectations to the chat.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the mutual action plan link and pre-read.

Best,

Alex / Clara —

Quick answers up front, then I’ll hand to Marcus for the deeper technical details in the call: 

Q1 (Dedicated data residency): Dedicated capacity provides hardware isolation at the pool level and we do not commingle customer model weights or inference KV caches. However, control-plane diagnostics (k8s-style traces and some aggregated metrics) are retained in Redwood logs to support operational support; we can discuss redaction/limited access controls. Backups of customer data are not taken by default.

Q2 (Private VPC control plane split): Private VPC option places the inference nodes and network egress inside your VPC; a lightweight control plane agent connects to Redwood’s control plane over a mutually authenticated channel. This means keys, audit logs, and network egress can be confined to Clearline’s network per your policy.

Q3 (Timeline / effort): Private VPC onboarding is typically 4–6 weeks for enterprise customers (network review, IAM/KMS integration, test deployment). Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in 1–2 weeks once procurement is finalized.

Ballpark pricing note (very rough): for an 8 GPU-month baseline, Dedicated monthly commit is usually ~X (we’ll put formal numbers in the MDP). Private VPC adds one-time onboarding fees and networking egress considerations — Marcus will follow up with an itemized checklist.

Marcus — can you join Wed 6/17 10:00am PT? I’ll send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan link.

Best,
Nikhil

Alex / team —

Short technical note ahead of Wed’s session so we can focus:

1) Private VPC (recommended for PHI):
   - Inference nodes run in your VPC/subnet; no egress to public internet unless you configure NAT.
   - Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported (AWS KMS, CloudHSM; bring-your-own-key flows).
   - Audit logs are written to your AWS CloudWatch/S3 endpoints or pushed to your SIEM — Redwood does not retain copies unless explicitly enabled.
   - Control plane agent uses mTLS with mutual auth; we provide a small footprint agent and a terraform module for reproducible networking.

2) Dedicated capacity (suitable for sensitive but non-PHI or where VPC setup is constrained):
   - Dedicated GPU pools are reserved for your account; compute is single-tenant but control plane operations (update orchestration, aggregated metrics) remain on Redwood’s control plane.
   - We can offer RBAC and least-privilege access for support engineers and provide tighter retention windows for logs; however, full KMS ownership and on-VPC-only egress require Private VPC.

3) Docs we’ll provide in advance of the call: redwood-privacy-matrix.csv (mapping of telemetry/log classes and retention), redwood-arch-diagram.png, SOC2-Summary.pdf.

4) Pre-call checklist for Clearline (helps us scope the config):
   - Desired KMS/HSM provider and key rotation policy.
   - Subnet/CIDR allocation and egress rules.
   - Compliance auditors who may require access (we’ll need to arrange an NDA + auditor connectivity plan).

I’ve tentatively booked Wed 6/17 10:00am PT for a 45-min deep-dive. Calendar invite with dial-in and the mutual action plan link coming from Nikhil.

— Marcus
